Rashi on Pesachim 89b:10:1.hebrew: ש"מ - אין רשאין ליחלק:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:10:1.english: Learn from this - They are not permitted to divide [into separate groups].

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:12:1.english: All these objections - [The cases of] one who registers others, and the attendant.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:12:2.hebrew: איתיביה בני חבורה - מרישיה, דקתני "טול חלקך", ושני ליה: בההיא משום דלתקוני זביחה קבליה וכמדת איש אחד, אבל אנא, צוותא קבילת עלך וניחא עלך צוותי לקבולי עלך בכל סעודתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:12:2.english: He raised an objection [from] "members of a group" - From its beginning, which teaches, "Take your portion," and he answered him: In that [case], it is because he accepted him [only] for the preparation of the sacrifice and according to the measure of one person; but [as for] me, you accepted [my] companionship upon yourself, and my companionship was pleasing to you to accept [me] upon yourself for my entire meal.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:1.hebrew: ועל חגיגתו - חגיגת י"ד, שאף היא באה לכל המנויין:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:1.english: And for his Festival peace-offering - [This refers to] the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan], for it too comes for all those registered.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:2.english: The money in his hand - That he took from these registrants.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:3.hebrew: חולין - כדמפרש טעמא לקמיה, שאף על פי שהנמנה כבר הקדיש מעותיו לכך והממנה כבר הקדיש פסחו, מתחללין המעות על הפסח, וטעמא מפרש:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:3.english: Non-sacred - As [the Gemara] explains the reason further on, that even though the one being registered already consecrated his money for this [purpose] and the one registering [him] already consecrated his Paschal offering, the money is deconsecrated onto the Paschal offering, and [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:4.hebrew: המוכר עולתו - להתכפר בה אחר, לא עשה כלום, ואין העולה קריבה אלא לשם בעלים הראשונים:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:4.english: One who sells his burnt-offering - For another [person] to achieve atonement through it, he has not done anything, and the burnt-offering is offered only for the sake of the original owners.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:5.hebrew: ומעות כל שהן - כל מה שקיבל מן העולה והשלמים, ואפילו יותר על כדי דמיהן, יפלו המעות לנדבת ציבור לשופרות שהיו במקדש, שהיו מקריבין מהן עולות לקיץ המזבח. ולקמיה פריך: מאחר דלא עשה ולא כלום, אמאי יפלו דמיהן לנדבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:14:5.english: And any money - Whatever he received for the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, even [if it is] more than their value, the money shall go to the communal free-will offering [fund], into the horn-shaped chests that were in the Temple, from which they would sacrifice burnt-offerings for the "dessert" of the altar [when it was idle]. And later [the Gemara] asks: Since he has not done anything, why should their value go to a free-will offering?

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:15:1.hebrew: אמר רבא קנסא - קנסו רבנן לקונה דלא ליקני זימנא אחריתי עולה ושלמים דאחר, ואיהו הוא דאפסיד אנפשיה, דלא הוה ליה למיקני כפרת אחרים. וכי האי גוונא נמי אמרי אינשי: לאו עכברא גנב אלא חורא גנב, כלומר, המוכר לא פשע אלא הקונה, הלכך מעותיו נדבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:15:1.english: Rava said: It is a fine - The Sages fined the buyer so that he will not buy another's burnt-offering or peace-offering another time, and it is he who caused himself the loss, for he should not have bought another's atonement. And regarding a case like this as well, people say: "The mouse is not the thief; rather, the hole is the thief" — that is to say, the seller was not at fault, rather the buyer [was]; therefore, his money [goes to] free-will offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:15:2.hebrew: אף על גב דשויא ארבעה ויהבו ליה ה' - לא אמר אישתכח דמתנה בעלמא הוא דיהב ליה, ולא ליקנסיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:15:2.english: Even though it was worth four [zuz] and they gave him five - [One] does not say [that] it turns out that it is merely a gift that he gave him, and [the Sages] should not fine him.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:16:1.english: Is it possible [that they] know, etc. - Would that they knew this reason and would inform us [of it].

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:16:2.hebrew: היאך - מעות הקדש חל על טלה הקדש אחר, לצאת הקדש של מעות לחולין? מי הוציאן למעות (של חולין)? אילו היה נותנן בבהמת חולין, היתה נתפסת בקדושת המעות והן יצאו לחולין; אבל עכשיו, מה נתפס תחתיהם שיצאו הם לחולין? והא ליכא למימר במעות שלא הוקדשו עסקינן, דאם כן מאי למימרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:16:2.english: How - [does] consecrated money take effect upon another consecrated lamb, so that the sanctity of the money goes out to non-sacred [status]? Who brought the money out (to non-sacred [status])? If he had given them for a non-sacred animal, [the animal] would be seized with the sanctity of the money and [the coins] would go out to non-sacred [status]; but now, what is seized in their place so that they should go out to non-sacred [status]? And one cannot say [that] we are dealing with unconsecrated money, for if so, what [need would there be] to state [it]?

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:1:1.hebrew: הממנה אחרים על פסחו - א' מבני חבורה שהמנה אחרים עמו על חלקו בלא דעת חבורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:1:1.english: One who registers others for his Paschal lamb - One of the members of a group who registered others with him on his portion without the knowledge of the group.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:1:2.hebrew: רשאין - לומר לו: טול חלקך וצא ואכול אתה וחבורתך את חלקך, דאית ליה להאי תנא פסח נאכל בב' חבורות:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:1:2.english: Are permitted - to say to him: "Take your portion and go out and eat, you and your group, your portion," for this Tanna holds [that] a Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:2:1.hebrew: ידיו יפות - לישנא מעליא, ממהר לאכול הרבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:2:1.english: His hands are fine - [This is] a euphemism [for one who] hastens to eat a lot.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:2:2.english: You accepted - You accepted me upon yourselves to eat with all my strength for this money.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:2:3.hebrew: לתקוני זביחה - שלא יהא נותר, ושיערנוך למאכל שאר בני אדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:2:3.english: For the preparation of the offering - So that there should not be leftover [meat], and we estimated you [according] to the eating of other people.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:3:1.english: Is it not because it is, etc. - That they will be eating with him.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:4:1.hebrew: דעות שאני - אין בני חבורה מרוצין להיות כל אלו הדעות בחבורתם, שמא יעכבו עליהם הסעודה. ולא משום אכילה יתירתא, אלא אפילו לא אכלי כולהו אלא כחד גברא, מצו מעכבי עליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:4:1.english: Minds are different - The members of the group are not willing to have all these minds in their group, lest they delay the meal for them. And [it is] not because of excessive eating; rather, even [if] all of them eat only like one person, they can object to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:5:1.hebrew: ממלא כריסו ממנו - כדאמרי' בכיצד צולין (לעיל פסחים דף פו.), שאין האוכל אוכל בשתי מקומות:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:5:1.english: He fills his stomach with it - As we say in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (above, Pesachim 86a), that one who eats may not eat in two places.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:5:2.hebrew: לא רצו לא - אלמא משום טירחא הדרי ביה, הכא נמי משום פסידא הדרי ביה. ומשני: לאטרחינן לדידך לא קבלינך. אבל ידיו יפות, מדלא בדקו אחריו, ש"מ בכל מאכלו קיבלו עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:5:2.english: [If] they did not want [to do so], no - Thus, because of the inconvenience they can retract; here too, because of the [financial] loss they can retract. [And the Gemara answers that they say to him:] We did not accept you so that we should trouble ourselves for you. However, [in the case of one with] fine hands, since they did not investigate him [beforehand], learn from this that they accepted him for whatever he eats.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:6:1.hebrew: לאטרחינן לדידך לא קבלינך - אבל ידיו יפות, מדלא בדקו אחריו, ש"מ בכל מאכלו קיבלו עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:6:1.english: To exert ourselves for you, we did not accept you - But [as for one whose] hands are fine [i.e., a fast eater], since they did not check after him [beforehand], learn from this [that] they accepted him for all his eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:7:1.english: Sibolet - [A] commingled meal of all the days of the year.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:8:1.english: What [is] "And not only"? - What is the greater strength of this [case] over that [case]?

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:8:2.english: For the preparation of the offering - [To eat] according to the measure of one person.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:8:3.english: Which is for companionship - And one might say [that] because of companionship, [they] accepted him upon themselves for whatever he eats.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:9:1.hebrew: רשאין ליחלק - לחלק פסח ביניהן, לכל א' חלק המגיעו:
Rashi on Pesachim 89b:9:1.english: Permitted to divide up - To divide the Paschal offering among themselves, [giving] each one the portion due to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 89b:9:2.english: Or are they not permitted to divide [it] - Rather, they eat together and the portions are placed before them like [at] other meals.

Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:14:1.hebrew: מעות כל שהן יפלו לנדבה - ק"ק לר"י, דרישא מיירי כשהקדיש מעות לשם פסח כדמוכח בסמוך, וסיפא מיירי במעות חולין; דאי הקדישן לשלמים, איך יפלו מעות שלמים לנדבת ציבור ויקריבו מהן עולות לקיץ המזבח:
Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:14:1.english: "Any money shall go for free-will offerings" - It is somewhat difficult for the Ri that the first clause [of the baraita] is speaking of when [the buyer] consecrated the money for the sake of a Paschal offering, as is proven shortly [in the Gemara], whereas the latter clause is speaking of non-sacred money; for if [the buyer] had consecrated them for peace-offerings, how could money [designated for] peace-offerings go to a communal free-will offering and burnt-offerings be sacrificed from them for the supplementation of the altar [kayitz hamizbe'ach]?

Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:15:1.hebrew: ומאחר דלא עשה ולא כלום אמאי יפלו לנדבה - פירוש: אי אמרת בשלמא דעשייתו מועלת, אתי שפיר דקנסינן ליה שלא ירגיל לעשות כן פעם אחרת; אבל כיון דלא עשה ולא כלום, אמאי קנסינן ליה כיון שאין ממש בעשייתו? ומשני דמ"מ קנסינן ליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:15:1.english: "And since he has not done anything, why should [the money] fall to free-will offerings?" - Explanation: Granted, if you say that his action is effective, it works out well that we fine him so that he will not make a habit of doing so another time; but since he has not done anything, why do we fine him, given that there is no substance to his action? And [the Gemara] answers that we fine him nevertheless.

Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:16:1.hebrew: וזה הפריש מעות לפסחו כו' - דאי במעות חולין, מאי קמ"ל? פשיטא שהן חולין, דלית לן למיקנסיה כמו בסיפא, כיון דשרי למנות אחרים על פסחו. וא"ת: אפילו אי הוו מעות חולין מעיקרא, מכל מקום איך יכול למנות אחרים אחר שהקדישו, כיון דסבר דאפילו במעות לא משייר — וכ"ש בפסח דלא משייר, מדקשיא ליה: אין הקדש חל על הקדש? וי"ל, דאע"ג דלא משייר ביה מידי, על דעת כן מקדישו, שיצאו כל אשר ימנה עליו; דקרא כתיב (שמות י״ב:ד׳): "ולקח הוא ושכנו", וכתיב ביה (שם): "תכוסו", משמע דבכל ענין, אפילו הקדישו כבר, משום דדעת האדם כן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:16:1.english: "And this [person] designated money for his Paschal lamb, etc." - For if [the baraita were speaking] of non-sacred money, what is it teaching us? It is obvious that it is non-sacred, for we have no reason to fine him as in the latter clause [of the baraita], since it is permitted to register others on one's Paschal lamb. And if you ask: Even if the money was non-sacred originally, nevertheless, how can he register others after he has consecrated [the lamb], since [Ulla] holds that even with money he does not leave over [any non-sacred portion] — and all the more so with a Paschal lamb, that he does not leave over [any non-sacred portion], since he has the difficulty [that] sanctity cannot take effect upon sanctity? One can answer: Even though he does not leave over anything [non-sacred] in it, it is with this intention that he consecrates it, that all whom he registers upon it shall fulfill [their obligation]; for Scripture writes (Exodus 12:4): "then he and his neighbor shall take," and it is written therein (ibid.): "you shall count," implying [that this applies] in any case, even if he has already consecrated it, because such is a person's intention.

Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:4:1.hebrew: דעות שאני - אע"ג דלא אכלי כולהו אלא כחד. תימה לר"י: מה צריך לשנויי הכי? לימא ליה דשאני הכא, דלא שייך למימר "הא קבילתון", ולא דמי כלל לידיו של א' מהן יפות! וי"ל דאיצטריך לשנויי הכי, דלא נידוק [איפכא דוקא] ממנה אחרים דלא מצי למימר "הא קבילתון", [הא ידיו יפות דמצי למימר "קבילתון"] אין רשאין ליתן חלקו. ומעיקרא דהוה בעי למיפשט דהוי כידיו של א' מהן יפות, ה"מ למפרך: "אדרבה, איפכא מסתברא!" לכך משני דלא מצי למיפשט מידי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:4:1.english: Minds are different - Even though all of them together eat only as [much as] one [person]. It is surprising to Rabbi Yitzchak: Why was it necessary [for the Gemara] to answer thus? Let it say [simply] that here it is different, because [the claim of] "You accepted me" does not apply, and it is not at all comparable to [the case where] one of them has fine hands! And one can say that it was necessary to answer thus so that we would not infer [the opposite: specifically] in the case of one who registers others, where he cannot say "You accepted me," [are they permitted to give him his portion; whereas in the case of one with fine hands, where he can say "You accepted me,"] they are not permitted to give him his portion. And initially, when [the Gemara] sought to resolve [the dilemma by comparing it] to [the case where] one of them has fine hands, one could have objected: "On the contrary, the opposite is more reasonable!" Therefore, it answers [that minds are different] so that one cannot resolve anything [from this Mishnah].

Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:9:1.hebrew: בני חבורה רשאין לחלק או לא - וא"ת, אמאי לא פשיט ממתני', דדוקא אם המנה האחרים עמו רשאין ליתן חלקו? וי"ל, דאיכא למידחי דבלא ממנה נמי רשאין ליחלק, והא דנקט ממנה — משום דבכל ענין מיירי, אפי' התנו שלא ליחלק, ואם ממנה רשאין ליחלק. אבל ברייתא לא מצי למידחי, דפשיטא דאם התנו שלא ליחלק, אפי' א' מהם ידיו יפות אין רשאין ליתן חלקו; דמסתמא על דעת כן התנו, דאם אין אחד מהן ידיו יפות, אין דרך ליחלק בלא תנאי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 89b:9:1.english: Are members of a group permitted to divide up or not - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not resolve [this] from the Mishnah, [which implies] that specifically if he registered others with him, they are permitted to give [him] his portion? One can answer that it is possible to deflect [this proof by saying] that even without registering [others], they are permitted to divide up, and that which [the Mishnah] stated "if he registered [others]" is because it is speaking of every case—even if they stipulated not to divide up, [nevertheless] if he registered [others], they are permitted to divide up. However, [the proof from] the Baraita cannot be deflected [in this manner], because it is obvious that if they stipulated not to divide up, even if one of them has fine hands, they are not permitted to give [him] his portion; for presumably it was with this intent that they stipulated, since if none of them has fine hands, it is not usual to divide up even without a stipulation.
